Keep the minimal balanced, p-adic family and characteristic-zero higher-Hida branches distinct, and expose every unresolved proof gate and supplier contract.

nodes.title: Nondegenerate ordinary roots
nodes.statement: For a field k and α,β ∈ k, NondegenerateOrdinaryRoots(α,β) means (α²−1)(β²−1)(α−β)(α²β²−1) ≠ 0. In arithmetic uses α,β are specified units, not merely an unordered pair of roots. This is the CG20 condition; it is stronger than α≠β and is unrelated to the regular-semisimple condition at an auxiliary prime.
proofSteps: Define the product on the existing field carrier; derive the four nonvanishing factors using absence of zero divisors.
Show invariance under exchanging the two roots and under injective field extension.
acceptance: Expose all four exclusions and preserve the distinction between units at p and four auxiliary eigenvalues.

nodes.title: Weight and Frobenius dictionary
nodes.statement: Use ε of Hodge–Tate weight −1 and geometric Frobenius throughout the CG branch. Its bundle ω(a,b) is the supplied rank-two Hodge bundle representation Sym^(a−b)⊗det^b. Pilloni’s Ω(k,r) is ω(k+r,r), with infinity parameter λ=(1−k−r,2−r;k+2r). In BCGP25, scalar weight two corresponds to λ=(1,1;2) and central character |·|²; its overconvergent Galois convention is dual-spin ρπ∨ε⁻³. Import the good-prime spin/dual-spin and full multiplier conversion from the current upstream Hecke roadmap, preserving every central operator.
proofSteps: Compute the highest weight of the Hodge bundle representation and compare each infinity-parameter convention.
Use the upstream dual/twist and full multiplier identities rather than rediscover the spin polynomial.
Keep the correction to the first infinity-coordinate sign explicit in the source ledger.
acceptance: Test Ω(0,2)=ω(2,2) and its λ=(−1,0;4) in the Pilloni convention; it is not literally BCGP’s λ without its separate normalization.
Record the precise conversion on polynomials and the full central character, even at trace zero.

sources.match: P20 §5.3 (p.24) defines Ω(k,r) as Sym^k⊗det^r of the Hodge bundle, so of highest weight (k+r,r), and the proof of Theorem 5.3.1 (p.25) gives the infinity parameter (1−k−r,2−r;k+2r) (the display on p.24 misprints the first entry). CG20 Remarks 5.10–5.11 (pp.833–834) identify ω(a,b) with the Levi weight (a,b;3−a−b) for the ν⁻³-twisted Hecke action. BCGP25 §1.8.12 (p.12) fixes central character |·|², Definition 1.8.16 (p.13) calls λ=(1,1;2) weight two, and Lemma 4.12.1 (p.112) defines ρ_f as the interpolation of ρ_π∨⊗ε⁻³. Together these give the dictionary recorded here.

nodes.title: Nonregular lifting data
nodes.statement: A CG lifting datum consists of an odd prime p≥5, a finite extension E/Qp with integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k; an integer a with p−1>a≥2; a continuous absolutely irreducible odd residual representation r̄:GQ→GSp₄(k) with multiplier ε̄^(1−a); chosen nondegenerate roots α,β; and a local basis at p with diagonal λ(α),λ(β),ε̄^(1−a)λ(β⁻¹),ε̄^(1−a)λ(α⁻¹), zero (1,2) and (3,4) entries and an unramified isotropic two-plane. It also records CG20 Assumptions 4.1–4.3, the minimal local deformation conditions and a chosen nonzero cuspidal residual eigensystem. The generic deformation functors, representations and pairings are supplied objects, not new definitions here.
proofSteps: Use the supplier representation, pairing and deformation objects and impose this particular conjunction of conditions.

Keep three image conditions separate: Q(ad⁰r̄) excludes ζp; for every m there is σ∈GQ(ζpᵐ) with four distinct roots and eigenvalue 1 on each irreducible adjoint constituent; the images of ad⁰r̄ and ad⁰r̄(1) have no quotient of order p.

Record away-p types U₁,U₂,U₃ by unipotent monodromy ranks 1,2,3; P by two isotropic inertia-character planes with x−1 prime to p; H by absolutely irreducible inertia with x⁴−1 prime to p. Under the fixed cyclotomic multiplier the P case is empty.

The local minimal functor fixes the full multiplier, preserves those inertia conditions and, at p, has the split unramified two-plane with characters lifting the specified roots, as in Definition 4.6. Representability remains a supplier obligation.
acceptance: Do not replace Assumption 4.1 by adequacy, or the selected ordinary plane by an arbitrary filtration.
The multiplier is ε^(1−a), with ε of Hodge–Tate weight −1 and geometric Frobenius ε(Frobℓ)=ℓ⁻¹.

nodes.title: Minimal tame levels and the neat auxiliary prime
nodes.statement: From a CG lifting datum satisfying Assumption 4.2 choose q≥3, q∉S(r̄)∪{p}, with q≠1 mod p and no ratio of residual Frobenius eigenvalues equal to q. At U₁,U₂,U₃ primes choose respectively paramodular, Klingen and Iwahori level; at P choose strict Klingen level; at H choose full congruence level at x; impose full level q and hyperspecial level elsewhere. For Q disjoint from S(r̄)∪{p,q}, form K₀(Q) and K₁(Q) (Klingen Π(x) and Π(x)⁺ at x∈Q), the group ΔQ=∏x∈Q(Z/xZ)^× of the étale cover X₁(Q)→X₀(Q) (through Π(x)/Π(x)⁺≅(Z/xZ)^×), and the intermediate cover XΔ(Q) for any quotient Δ of ΔQ; the patching argument uses quotients of p-power order. The prime q makes these moduli problems neat.
proofSteps: Choose the Frobenius class by Chebotarev from the stated neatness witness, then choose a prime outside the finite excluded set.
Use the suppliers for integral models, compatible fans and bundles; specify the local compact subgroups and their Klingen-character kernels.
The no-eigenvalue-ratio condition gives H²(Qq,ad⁰r̄)=0 and forces every relevant lift to be unramified at q.
acceptance: State the auxiliary-prime unramifiedness for the lift itself, and identify the trivial Q cover with the base level.

sources.match: CG20 Assumption 4.2 (p.813) asks for σ with ε(σ)=q≢1 mod p and no ratio of eigenvalues of r̄(σ) equal to q. §6.3 (pp.840–841) picks such a prime q by Chebotarev away from p and the bad primes, and sets K_x to the Iwahori I(x), Klingen Π(x), paramodular K(x), Π(x)⁺ or full level x for types U3, U2, U1, P, H, with full level at q. §5.2 (pp.821–822) defines K₀(Q), K₁(Q) and the étale cover X₁(Q)→X₀(Q) with group Δ_Q=∏(Z/x)^×, and §7.2 (p.851) the intermediate covers X_Δ(Q). The proof of Theorem 6.13 (p.843) shows all lifts are unramified at q because H²(Q_q,ad⁰r̄)=0. Neatness of full level q needs q≥3 (CG20 extraction E57).

nodes.title: Klingen Taylor–Wiles refinements
nodes.statement: A CG Taylor–Wiles refinement at x∉S∪{p} consists of x≡1 mod pᴺ, four distinct residual Frobenius roots (αx,βx,γx,δx), two specified complementary isotropic planes, the pairing labels αxδx=βxγx=ν(Frobx), and the extra separation αxβx≠γxδx. Roots lift uniquely in the appropriate henselian Hecke factor. The pairing labels and product separation are additional requirements, not consequences of the two isotropic planes.
proofSteps: Use the supplier auxiliary-prime theorem with the precise CG image hypothesis, not a dimension-general theorem with different assumptions.
Label roots respecting the symplectic pairing, and exchange βx and γx when necessary to get the product separation.
Track the chosen isotropic plane through scalar inertia deformations.
acceptance: Keep the one-dimensional Klingen diamond factor here distinct from the two-dimensional torus factor in NR10.

Assumption 7.1 (p.846) repeats this on the Hecke side, and Theorem 7.2 (p.847) forms R_x from the products α′γ′, β′δ′, γ′δ′, which isolates the αβ-block only when α_xβ_x≠γ_xδ_x (CG20 extraction E67). nodes.statement: For the supplied cuspidal coherent sections H⁰(X₁(Q),ω(μ)(−D)⊗E/O), define Tanμ(Q) as the O-subalgebra image generated by spherical operators away from S∪Q∪{p}; Tμ(Q) adds Ux,i and ΔQ; T̃μ(Q) adds the integral p-operators Tp,1 and Qp,2=(pTp,2+(p+p³)Sp)p^(2−b) for μ=(a,b). Restrict these actual images to the invariant X₀(Q) subspace when that level is used. Define ordinary images by restriction to the invertible Tp,1Qp,2 summand, rather than by simply adjoining inverses to an unrelated ring.
proofSteps: Import abstract Hecke images, spin-polynomial normalizations and factorial projectors; specify the generating double cosets and their actual action.
Require the integral geometric construction of normalized p-operators before using their image; Fourier identities alone do not define higher-degree actions.
Prove the X₀(Q) subspace is stable and that the three ring maps are induced by their common faithful image action.

nodes.title: Joint ordinary root selectors
nodes.statement: On a finite O-Hecke algebra, with its adic topology, or compatibly on its finite quotients, let e(T,c)=1−limn(T−c)^(n!) be the generalized c-root selector. The two complementary limits are multiplied separately; taking one complement of their product selects an incorrect union.

Use commuting p-operators to multiply commuting idempotents and identify the image with the intersection.

nodes.title: Coefficient fields of coherent eigensystems
nodes.statement: Let K be neat and Ω(k,r)=ω(k+r,r), k≥0, r∈Z, on the Siegel threefold. Every simultaneous characteristic-zero Hecke character Θ occurring in any finite-dimensional Hⁱ of its canonical or subcanonical extension has values in a number field E. For every λ|p choose an embedding E→Q̄p. Finite-dimensionality is used for this actual Hecke image, so an arbitrary character of a free algebra is not covered.
proofSteps: Use the rational structure on the algebraic variety and bundle, finite coherent cohomology and the rational Hecke action.
The image of the commutative Hecke algebra in EndQ(Hⁱ) is finite-dimensional; the residue field of its characteristic-zero character is finite over Q.
Identify all eigenvalues with this common finite field and transport along each chosen p-adic embedding.
acceptance: Treat both extension conventions and each degree; do not appeal only to a coefficient-field theorem for classical H⁰ forms.

nodes.title: No Steinberg component in scalar weight two
nodes.statement: If π is the cuspidal automorphic representation of a classical Siegel form of weight (2,2), then no finite local component is Steinberg in the source’s normalized central-character convention. At a Steinberg place x, the normalized Ux,1 eigenvalue in weight (j,k) is x^((j+k−6)/2), and in weight (2,2) it is x⁻¹, contradicting integrality of the Fourier-normalized Hecke action. Include any allowed finite unramified unit twist in the local calculation; its valuation does not change the contradiction.
proofSteps: Request the local Steinberg parameter and its U-eigenvalue in the exact geometric normalization from the GSp₄ local representation supplier.
Establish integrality of the action on the Fourier lattice and hence integrality of its eigenvalue.
At the residue characteristic x the proposed Steinberg eigenvalue has negative valuation; conclude it cannot occur.
acceptance: The proof is an integral Hecke-eigenvalue obstruction, not a consequence of an unproved association of an abelian variety to every weight-two form.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.9 and proof, p.832
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 5.9 (p.832) states that no local component of a cuspidal automorphic representation attached to a weight-(2,2) Siegel form is Steinberg. Its proof computes the U_{x,1}-eigenvalue x^{(w−3)/2} with w=j+k−3, which is x⁻¹ in weight (2,2), contradicting integrality of Hecke eigenvalues.

nodes.title: All-degree characteristic-zero interpolation
nodes.statement: For the characteristic-zero coherent eigensystems of NR2, the away-p Hecke action factors continuously through the inverse limit of finite free integral Hecke images on cuspidal H⁰ at varying p-levels and finite sets of regular weights. The resulting continuous semisimple ρΘ,λ:GQ→GL₄(Q̄p) is unramified outside Np and satisfies det(1−XρΘ,λ(Frobℓ))=Θ(Qℓ(X)) at ℓ∤Np. This applies to every coherent degree and both canonical and subcanonical extensions. It does not identify the unusual integral models in Pilloni–Stroh with a chosen Kottwitz lattice.
proofSteps: Import the geometric interpolation input for the modified ample Hodge bundle: Hodge–Tate sections give a Hecke-stable cover, and Čech localization modulo pˢ reduces classes to sections.
Clear denominators with high powers, use positivity and Serre vanishing to lift regular-weight sections, and pass through the finite integral Hecke images.
Use duality for the other extension convention; reconstruct the semisimple representation from the continuous determinant and good-prime identities.
Record an independent lattice-comparison obligation before applying this theorem to a specific torsion integral lattice.
acceptance: Do not infer CG20 Lemma 6.9 for its torsion lattice solely from this characteristic-zero theorem.
Symplectic descent and de Rhamness are separate conclusions requiring their own hypotheses.

sources.locator: Theorem 0.1, pp.1–2; Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.10, pp.16–17; Corollary 3.14, p.19; P20 Theorem 5.3.1, author p.25
sources.match: PS16 Theorem 0.1 (pp.1–2) and Theorem 3.6 (p.16) show that the Hecke action on any coherent H^i of ω^κ or ω^κ(−D) factors continuously through the p-adic Hecke algebra, the inverse limit over p-levels and finite sets of weights of the finite free Z_p-algebras acting on cuspidal H⁰. Remark 3.10 (pp.16–17) notes that their integral structures differ from the lattice of the Kottwitz model. Corollary 3.14 (p.19) deduces the GL₄-valued Galois representation of a genus-two coherent eigensystem with the unramified characteristic-polynomial identity, and P20 Theorem 5.3.1 (p.25) uses this in every degree.

nodes.title: Qualified crystalline specialization
nodes.statement: For a simple-generic cuspidal GSp₄ representation over a totally real field with archimedean parameter φ(w,m₁,m₂), m₁>m₂≥0 and w+1≡m₁+m₂ mod 2, assume spherical level at every v|p and four distinct inverse Hecke roots there. Under the classification hypotheses, Mok’s associated p-adic representation is crystalline at v|p, hence de Rham, including the stated limit-of-discrete-series cases. This theorem does not assert de Rhamness for every ordinary singular coherent eigensystem.
proofSteps: Use the finite-slope family and crystalline-period continuation with its distinct-root hypothesis from the supplier geometric Galois construction.
Carry the central character and archimedean parity through the weight dictionary.
Apply coefficient extension and de Rham descent from the period-functor API.
acceptance: A repeated-root ordinary representation is outside this specialization; do not remove the distinct inverse-root condition.

sources.locator: §4, Theorem 4.14 and Proposition 4.16, pp.40–42; P20 §5.3, author pp.25–26
sources.match: M14 §4 (p.24) assumes holomorphic discrete series or limits of discrete series at infinity with parameter φ(w,m₁,m₂), m₁>m₂≥0, w+1≡m₁+m₂ mod 2. Theorem 4.14 (p.40) gives the semisimple R_p for a simple generic parameter, with local–global compatibility up to semisimplification, and Proposition 4.16 (p.42) states that R_p is crystalline at a spherical v|p when the inverse roots of Q_{Π,v} are distinct. P20 §5.3 (pp.25–26) cites this for de Rhamness.

nodes.title: Ordinary weight-two Galois representation
nodes.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split, and let π be an ordinary cuspidal weight-two GSp₄(A_F⁺) representation in the BCGP25 convention λ=(1,1;2), with central character |·|². There is a continuous semisimple ρπ:G_F⁺→GSp₄(Q̄p), multiplier ε⁻¹. Away from p its Weil–Deligne semisimplification equals recGT(πv|ν|^(−3/2))ss. At v|p it is upper triangular with diagonal α,β,β⁻¹ε⁻¹,α⁻¹ε⁻¹, where α and β are potentially unramified. Neither full monodromy equality nor de Rhamness follows from this basic interpolation statement.
proofSteps: Use the ordinary families with dense regular classical points and the fixed central-character identity.
Interpolate the symplectic Galois object; at p retain the four ordered ordinary characters and potential unramifiedness.

Apply the semisimplified local comparison with its explicit |ν| twist. When ρπ is irreducible, the ε⁻¹-line in ∧²ρπ gives a nondegenerate alternating pairing; in general the GSp₄-valued output comes from GSp₄ pseudocharacters (recorded gap).
acceptance: The statement is over Q̄p, so no integral descent is involved, also at p=2; the GSp₄-valued interpolation uses Lafforgue's GSp₄ pseudocharacters and their reconstruction over Q̄p.

sources.locator: §1.8.12, p.12; Definition 1.8.16 and Theorem 1.8.17, pp.13–14
sources.match: BCGP25 §1.8.12 (p.12) fixes central character |·|², Definition 1.8.16 (p.13) defines weight two as λ=(1,1;2) with a non-degenerate limit of discrete series at infinity, and Theorem 1.8.17 (pp.13–14) gives a semisimple GSp₄-valued ρ_{π,p} with multiplier ε⁻¹, local–global compatibility up to semisimplification away from p with the |ν|^{−3/2} twist (1.8.18), and an upper-triangular shape α,β,β⁻¹ε⁻¹,α⁻¹ε⁻¹ at p (1.8.19) with α,β potentially unramified. The proof interpolates GSp₄-valued pseudorepresentations over an ordinary eigenvariety.

nodes.title: Pure general-type monodromy upgrade
nodes.statement: In NR2/weight-two, if π is of general type and the corresponding ρπ is pure, upgrade the away-p comparison to an equality of Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representations retaining monodromy N. The general-type and purity assumptions are not omitted.
proofSteps: General type means the transfer to GL₄ is cuspidal, hence locally generic, so the L-packet of πv⊗|ν|^(−3/2) is generic; by the GSp₄ local Langlands correspondence of Gan–Takeda (main theorem, part vii) the adjoint L-factor of its parameter is holomorphic at s=1.

Purity of ρπ makes its Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation pure; by Taylor–Yoshida Lemma 1.4 a pure Weil–Deligne representation with the given semisimplification carries the unique monodromy compatible with that holomorphy, which is the monodromy of the automorphic side.
Keep the N-bearing comparison distinct from the basic semisimplified interpolation theorem.
acceptance: An unramified-trace identity alone cannot certify this target.
The adjoint input is local (holomorphy at s=1 of a local adjoint L-factor), not a global analytic statement.

sources.locator: Remark 1.8.20 and its argument, p.14
sources.match: BCGP25 Remark 1.8.20 (p.14) upgrades (1.8.18) to an equality of Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations with monodromy when π is of general type and ρ_{π,p} is pure. The argument is local: the L-packet of π_v⊗|ν|^{−3/2} is generic, so by Gan–Takeda's main theorem (part vii) its adjoint L-factor is holomorphic at s=1, and Taylor–Yoshida Lemma 1.4 then determines the monodromy of a pure representation.

nodes.title: Dual-spin overconvergent interpolation
nodes.statement: For an ordinary overconvergent eigenform f∈H⁰⁰_w(Sh_Kp,ω(2,2;−w),sm), with w even and smooth torus character χ=χ₁⊗χ₂⊗χ₃⊗χ₄, construct its semisimple GSp₄ representation ρf with good-prime polynomial Pℓ in BCGP25’s dual-spin convention: at classical points it is ρπ∨ε⁻³. Under local reciprocity the ordered p-diagonal characters on z∈Qp× are χ₄(z)⁻¹z^(−1−w/2), χ₃(z)⁻¹z^(−1−w/2), χ₂(z)⁻¹z^(−2−w/2), χ₁(z)⁻¹z^(−2−w/2). Specify the reciprocity convention on p as well as Zp×.
proofSteps: Import higher-Hida/overconvergent spaces and their local torus action.
Interpolate the dual-spin polynomial with the central operator and compare with the classical dual-and-twist formula.
Read the local characters from the ordered torus eigensystem, correcting the double inverse printed in the final two entries of BCGP25 Lemma 4.12.1.
acceptance: Never identify this dual-spin representation with the geometric-spin ρπ without the indicated dual and cyclotomic twist.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.12.1 and its proof, p.112; Remark 4.12.2, p.112
sources.match: BCGP25 Lemma 4.12.1 (p.112) attaches to an ordinary overconvergent eigenform f of weight (2,2;−w) a semisimple ρ_f with values in GSp₄, unramified outside S with P_ℓ mod m_f the characteristic polynomial of Frob_ℓ, and Borel-valued at p with diagonal given through class field theory on Z_p^× and on p; the last two diagonal entries are misprinted with a double inverse. Its proof defines ρ_f as the interpolation of ρ_{π,p}∨⊗ε⁻³, and Remark 4.12.2 explains this choice.

nodes.title: Completed eigenspace isotypy
nodes.statement: Let V=H³(RHom_b(λ,RΓ(Sh_Kp^tor,Qp)^la)^ord_mρ̄), λ=(1,1;w), with the algebraic torus character removed as in BCGP25. Assume residual absolute irreducibility, ρf irreducible, and either Zariski image containing Sp₄, or image containing SL₂×SL₂ with ρf becoming reducible on an index-two subgroup. For an occurring eigenform f, the eigenspace V[mf] is nonzero, finite-dimensional and isomorphic to ρf⊗W for a finite-dimensional nonzero multiplicity space W.
proofSteps: Use the four higher-Coleman graded pieces and exactness of χ-isotypic parts for smooth T(Zp)-modules in characteristic zero: (V⊗Cp)[χ] is finite-dimensional, with Gr⁰ the ordinary overconvergent H⁰.
The maximal ideal mf lies in the support of the finite-length module (V⊗Cp)[χ], through its quotient Gr⁰, so its mf-torsion is nonzero; no exactness of the eigenspace functor is needed.

Each Frobℓ satisfies Pℓ mod mf on V[mf] by the Eichler–Shimura relation. Apply the GSp₄ semisimplicity criteria for representations annihilated by the Frobenius characteristic polynomials of ρf (BCGP25 Propositions 4.11.1–4.11.2); the Cayley–Hamilton recognition of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants Layer 1.6 needs annihilation by the whole Cayley–Hamilton ideal and does not apply directly.
acceptance: The conclusion includes W≠0, not only a multiple-of-four dimension assertion.
Only the Frobenius characteristic polynomials are known to annihilate V[mf]; the image hypothesis is what makes this enough.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.12.3 and proof, p.113; Propositions 4.11.1–4.11.2, pp.109–110; Theorem 1.8.29, p.17
sources.match: BCGP25 Lemma 4.12.3 (p.113) shows, for irreducible ρ_f with either Sp₄ in the Zariski closure of the image or the induced SL₂×SL₂ case, that V[m_f]=ρ_f⊗W with W finite-dimensional and nonzero. The χ-isotypic part of V⊗C_p is finite-dimensional with the graded pieces of Theorem 4.9.9 and Gr⁰ equal to the ordinary overconvergent H⁰, so m_f lies in its support and V[m_f]≠0; isotypy then follows from the Eichler–Shimura relation (Theorem 1.8.29) and Propositions 4.11.1–4.11.2 (pp.109–110).

nodes.title: Hasse shifts and the vanishing threshold
nodes.statement: For μ=(a,b), use the supplied scalar Hasse invariant h of weight (p−1,p−1), a characteristic-zero lift A of hʳ with r>0, and a threshold N(μ) for higher-cohomology vanishing after a sufficiently positive scalar shift. For coefficients O/ϖᵐ choose s divisible by p^(m−1) with t=rs(p−1)≥N(μ), and set μ′=μ+(t,t). Multiplication by Aˢ is injective on sections and is equivariant for the normalized away-p Hecke action. Equivariance for the normalized p-operators is a separate assertion and is not inferred from this construction.
proofSteps: Import Hasse invariants, their lift and its finite-level congruences from the proposed Siegel modular-forms supplier.
Choose the shift using the supplied positivity/vanishing theorem, preserving the difference a−b.
Prove integral injectivity using that the multiplier is a nonzerodivisor on the appropriate model; identify precisely the operators with which it commutes.
acceptance: Track m and the divisibility of s; a lift merely congruent to hʳ modulo ϖ need not have the required equivariance modulo ϖᵐ.

sources.match: CG20 Definition 6.1 (p.836) fixes the Hasse invariant h and a lift A of h^r, Definition 6.3 (p.836) the vanishing threshold N(μ), and Lemma 6.4 (pp.836–837) chooses s divisible by p^{m−1} with t=rs(p−1)≥N(μ), so that multiplication by A^s is injective on H⁰ with O/ϖ^m coefficients and commutes with the operators away from p and the U_{x,i}. Remark 6.5 (p.837) records the induced surjection of Hecke algebras.

nodes.title: Selected annihilator quotients
nodes.statement: For the selected finite-level module Hμ,m^sel define Jμ,m^sel=Ann(Tμ^sel,Hμ,m^sel), and its enlarged-image counterpart. The regular-weight comparison uses the composite e′β∘Aˢ on the β-part. Once this composite is proved injective, it induces a surjection from the high-weight Hecke image to Tμ^sel/Jμ,m^sel for the operators whose actions intertwine. The target ideal is the annihilator of the selected module, not that of the full coherent module.
proofSteps: Define the annihilator using the actual action on the named summand.
For regular β-parts prove injectivity on the socle using the residual p-operator formulas, and then on the finite local module.
Factor the intertwining action through the image quotient; show surjectivity on the specified generating operators.
In singular weight postpone the corresponding injection until NR4/doubling-injection.
acceptance: Do not claim that Aˢ alone preserves the β-summand, or that the full p-characteristic-polynomial identity descends by away-p equivariance.

The proof of Theorem 6.13 (pp.842–843) restricts multiplication by A^s to β-parts and claims a surjection T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m→T_μ(Q)^β_m/I_{μ,m}. nodes.title: Central characters and residual Galois systems
nodes.statement: For every maximal ideal of the anemic image in NR1 there is a continuous semisimple residual GL₄ representation matching the good-prime spin polynomial. It is unique up to isomorphism; if absolutely irreducible, it has an alternating pairing and the full prescribed central multiplier, and is non-Eisenstein. Its pullbacks along T→T̃ and ordinary/selected image maps have the same residual representation. The central character is constructed independently from the full spherical central operators, not inferred from the determinant square.
proofSteps: Use the Hasse transfer of NR3 for finite-quotient residual systems, characteristic-zero regular eigenforms and the imported reconstruction theorem. The arrow to NR3 is a proof dependency; the statement is first available after NR3.

For simple-generic characteristic-zero systems use the alternating pairing theorem; in the reducible non-simple-generic cases specify each constituent and its pairing before reducing. Do not assert that reducibility itself implies symplecticity.
Interpolate the full central Hecke character and compare it with the representation multiplier; transport to the other image rings by the shared good polynomials.
acceptance: Keep Arthur/classification assumptions visible from Lemma 6.9 onward.
Absolute irreducibility, not irreducibility over the residue field alone, is required for the integral reconstruction and unique pairing.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.6, pp.837–838; Proposition 6.8 and Lemma 6.9, pp.838–840; Definition 6.11, p.840
sources.match: CG20 Proposition 6.6 (p.838) constructs the central character χ_μ with χ_μ(Frob_x)=S_x. Proposition 6.8 (pp.838–839) attaches to cuspidal eigenforms of regular weight semisimple GSp₄-valued r_f with multiplier λ_f∘χ_μ·ε⁻³ and characteristic polynomial Q_x. Lemma 6.9 (p.839) reduces these to residual GL₄ representations r̄_m for maximal ideals of T^an_μ(Q) and, through Arthur's transfer and Bellaïche–Chenevier, makes absolutely irreducible ones symplectic; Remark 6.10 extends this to T_μ(Q) and T̃_μ(Q), and Definition 6.11 (p.840) defines non-Eisenstein ideals.

nodes.title: Regular-weight Hecke-valued Galois representation
nodes.statement: For regular μ=(a,b), a≥b≥3, a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal with residual r̄, the prescribed tame level and labelled auxiliary primes, construct rβμ,m:GQ→GSp₄(Tμ(Q)β_m). It matches every good-prime spin polynomial away from S∪Q∪{p}; has multiplier χμ,0ε^(−(a+b−3)) with χμ,0 finite order and residually trivial; and is upper triangular at p with diagonal λ(dp,1), ε^(−(b−2))λ(dp,2), ε^(−(a−1))λ(dp,3), ε^(−(a+b−3))λ(dp,4), where dp,1≡β and dp,2≡α. After an odd-p square-root character twist it has the required weakly minimal away-p local conditions. The additional equality involving the complete Hecke polynomial at p is not included without a separate proof.
proofSteps: At high regular weight use vanishing, a torsion-free characteristic-zero eigenform decomposition and the supplied regular Galois representations. The Hecke image embeds into the product of their integer rings.

Import the regular-weight eigenform representations of CG20 Proposition 6.8 (existence, crystalline at p with Frobenius polynomial Qp, ordinary shape, symplectic pairing, local–global compatibility) from the automorphic Galois suppliers.
Descend traces and the full multiplier into the integral image by the upstream p>2 symplectic descent theorem; pass to selected finite-quotient image rings.
Obtain the ordered ordinary characters from the regular ordinary theory, carrying their four cyclotomic exponents.
Take the compatible inverse limit and use the unique finite-character square root congruent to 1 to fix the multiplier; verify weak minimality prime by prime, including unramifiedness at q.
acceptance: The proof must identify the local characters on the selected quotient; a p-polynomial identity requires more than a good-prime trace descent.
Do not use the unproved torsion-freeness expectation of Remark 6.14.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.13(1)–(4) and proof, pp.841–844, restricted to the assertions transported by the proof
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 6.13 (pp.841–842) constructs r^β_{μ,m} with values in GSp₄(T_μ(Q)^β_m) for regular μ=(a,b), a≥b≥3, under Assumption 6.12: multiplier χ_{μ,0}ε^{−(a+b−3)}, polynomial Q_x at good primes, units d_{p,i} with d_{p,1}≡β and d_{p,2}≡α and an upper-triangular ordinary shape at p, and weak minimality after a square-root twist. The proof (pp.842–843) passes to high weight, embeds the Hecke algebra in a product of integer rings using Proposition 6.8, descends using [CHT08] and [GG12], and checks the local conditions with [Sor10].

nodes.title: Formal operators in the doubling argument
nodes.statement: Work over k of odd characteristic p, with tame level prime to p and trivialized auxiliary Nebentypus, in weights (j,2) with j≥4 or j=2. Let q-series have coefficients in Sym^(j−2)(k²), indexed by p-integral positive-semidefinite binary forms Q with bounded tame denominators and the prescribed Γ-equivariance. Set a(UF;Q)=a(F;pQ). For integral representatives M of Γ diag(p,1) Γ, set a(ZF;Q)=ΣM Sym^(j−2)(M)a(F;M⁻¹·Q), interpreting nonintegral indices as zero, where M·Q=det(M)⁻¹MQMᵗ. Put Z₂=UZ and a(X₂F;Q)=(disc(Q)/p)a(F;Q). An integral binary-form index Q is p-primitive when its three coefficients are not all divisible by p; this is a condition on the index, not on a series over k.
proofSteps: Import the general Fourier-series, q-expansion and symmetric-power coefficient APIs from the proposed Siegel modular-forms supplier.
Define these specialized operators by the displayed finite sums and coefficient functions, and prove independence of the double-coset representatives.
Use the discriminant of the binary form consistently; the Legendre multiplier is zero when p divides the discriminant.
Prove Z₂X₂=0, UX₂=0 and X₂³=X₂ in characteristic p.
acceptance: Do not assert that every formal series is modular. The modularity of T and Q₂ is a separate supplied geometric result.

Lemma 8.4 (pp.858–859) expands T₂ and records Z₂=UZ, Definition 8.5 (p.859) defines X₂ through U₂=−1+pX₂ with a Legendre-symbol formula, Lemma 8.6 gives Z₂X₂=0 over k and Definition 8.7 defines p-primitive forms. §§8.1–8.2 (pp.856–857, Theorem 8.1 and Remark 8.2) set up the q-expansions and the weight range.

nodes.title: Theta operators with corrected weights
nodes.statement: Import the scalar theta operator Θ with Fourier multiplier det(Q) and its injectivity in the range 2≤k≤p+1, p∤k(2k−1), excluding k=p−1. Import the vector operator θ₁ from weight (j,k) to (j+p−1,k+p+1) with coefficient con(a(F;Q)⊗Q), with no extra determinant factor. For the doubling use p>3 and p−1>j≥4, where θ₁ is injective on the required modular forms. These are supplier theorems, recorded here as the precise specialization needed for the kernel argument.
proofSteps: Request the geometric theta construction and its holomorphy, weight and injectivity from SiegelModularFormsModPn.
Separate the scalar determinant multiplier from the vector contraction; the contraction is a nonzero integral transvectant in the valid coefficient range.
Test Θ on the Hasse invariant to exclude the erroneous k=p−1 case; for the scalar-weight argument use precisely k=p+1.
acceptance: The vector contraction has no determinant prefactor, and all stated theta identities are in characteristic p.

Theorem 8.10 (pp.861–862) asserts injectivity of Θ for k≤p+1 with p∤k(2k−1), which fails at k=p−1 for the Hasse invariant, and Theorem 8.11 (pp.862–863) asserts injectivity of θ₁ in weight (j,2) for p−1>j≥4.

nodes.statement: Let M be the q-expansions of the localized selected cuspidal weight-(j,2) k-space and let N be its Hasse embedding into a sufficiently regular modular-form space, viewed in the same formal coefficient space because h has expansion 1. Keep the finite-dimensional ambient Hecke-stable space and its U-generalized decomposition N=Nα⊕Nβ⊕N₀. Let πβ be the normalized idempotent projection onto Nβ. A power of U−α can have the same kernel in the relevant subspace, but is not defined to be πβ.
proofSteps: Use the q-expansion principle to regard Hasse multiplication as an inclusion of the same coefficient vectors.
Enlarge to a finite-dimensional U-stable modular space before discussing generalized eigenspaces.
Import the ordinary regular root calculation to prove that U(U−α)(U−β) acts nilpotently; use distinct α,β,0 to split N.
acceptance: The input M need not be U-stable; every use of U iteration must take place in its finite U-stable envelope.

nodes.title: Invertible Q₂ and the U-ordinary envelope
nodes.statement: For the spaces M⊂N of NR4, use T=U+Z and, in characteristic p and weight (j,2), Q₂=Z₂ for j>2 and Q₂=Z₂+X₂ for j=2. If Q₂ is invertible on M, then for j>2 M is contained in the U-invertible part of N. For j=2, Z₂ is injective on M and its image is contained in the U-invertible part. The proof uses W=Σi≥0UⁱM, which is finite-dimensional and U-stable, and Z₂W⊂UW.
proofSteps: Enlarge M to W and use UZ=Z₂ with commutation of U and Z₂ to obtain Z₂W⊂UW, then iterate inside W.
For j>2 use invertibility of Q₂=Z₂ to place M in ∩nUⁿW.
For j=2 use X₂³=X₂, Z₂X₂=0 and the eigenvalue Q₂=αβ with (αβ)²≠1 to deduce injectivity of Z₂, before applying the same envelope argument.
acceptance: Do not use Q₂-invertibility on a larger unrelated space; the envelope argument repairs the missing stability step.

sources.locator: Lemma 8.15 and proof, pp.867–868; Lemma 8.16, p.868
sources.match: CG20 Lemma 8.15 (pp.867–868) asserts that Q₂ is invertible on M and that M (Z₂M in weight (2,2)) lies in the U-invertible part of N; Lemma 8.16 (p.868) records the supporting operator identities. The proof iterates U before stability under U is known, which the node repairs with W=ΣU^iM (CG20 extraction E107).

nodes.title: Contraction on all Fourier indices
nodes.statement: For j≥4 in the theta range, prove the formal characteristic-p identity θ₁(ZF)=0 for every Γ-equivariant integral q-expansion of weight (j,2), including coefficients whose discriminant is divisible by p. This is the strengthened coefficient lemma needed to replace the incomplete all-coefficient step in CG20 Proposition 8.25. Its proof obligation is the integral transvectant equivariance identity: contraction of Sym^(j−2)(M)v against M·Q equals det(M) times the transported contraction of v against Q, in the exact dual-form convention, when det(M)=p.
proofSteps: Write the contraction in the chosen binary-form coordinates over Z localized away from the required factorial denominators.
Verify the GL₂ covariance with the precise determinant-normalized action on indices and the dual/contraction conventions; reduce modulo p only after clearing justified denominators.
Apply the identity term by term to the finite Z sum for every index, not only a minimal-discriminant coefficient.
If this covariance identity does not supply the asserted all-index annihilation, retain the target as a gap and supply a correct replacement for the doubling theorem.
acceptance: This target is a proof obligation, not a claimed new proof of Proposition 8.25.
A vanishing contraction at one chosen Fourier index does not imply θ₁F=0.

sources.locator: Proposition 8.25, contraction claim and proof, pp.876–877; Proposition 8.9, p.861
sources.match: CG20 Proposition 8.25 (pp.876–877) derives θ₁F=0 for F with UF=αF and ZF=βF in weight (j,2), j≥4, from a contraction computation at chosen Fourier indices, and Proposition 8.9 (p.861) gives the θ₁ coefficient formula. The node isolates the identity θ₁∘Z≡0 mod p at every index that the argument needs (design E11; CG20 extraction E95, E125).

nodes.title: The two constrained kernel systems
nodes.statement: A nonzero kernel of πβ∘h on the selected source yields a nonzero constrained vector after simultaneous finite-dimensional spectral reduction. For j>2, take F with UF=αF, TF=(α+β)F and hence ZF=βF. For j=2, write F=Fα+F₀ with UFα=αFα, UF₀=0, X₂F=αβF₀ and ZF=βF+αF₀, while Q₂F=αβF. These are consequences for a reduced kernel vector, not equalities asserted on every generalized eigenvector.
proofSteps: Use the commuting selected Hecke action on the nonzero kernel to pass to a simultaneous eigenvector over a splitting field.
In j>2 eliminate N₀ with the ordinary-envelope theorem and identify the remaining α-eigenvector.
In j=2 retain the zero-root component and derive its X₂ and Z relations from the formal operators; never discard F₀ without proof.
acceptance: The scalar-weight system contains the extra αF₀ term; omitting it would falsely simplify the hardest case.

sources.locator: Lemma 8.17 and proof, pp.868–871
sources.match: CG20 Lemma 8.17 (pp.868–871) reduces a nonzero vector in the kernel of π_β to one with UF=αF and ZF=βF when j>2, and in weight (2,2) to F=F_α+F₀ with UF_α=αF_α, X₂F=αβF₀ and ZF=βF+αF₀.

nodes.title: Vanishing of constrained cuspidal vectors
nodes.statement: Under the root condition and p−1>j≥4, a cuspidal vector satisfying UF=αF and ZF=βF vanishes, using NR4/contraction and theta injectivity. In weight (2,2), a cuspidal vector satisfying the full scalar system of NR4/kernel-equations also vanishes. The planned statement is restricted to cusp forms, so the minimal-discriminant argument starts with a positive-definite coefficient and does not assume a nonzero discriminant for an arbitrary noncuspidal series.
proofSteps: For j>2 use βθ₁F=θ₁ZF=0 and β≠0, then the imported vector theta injectivity. The all-index contraction obligation must be discharged first.

For the scalar case show coefficients at nonsquare discriminants vanish by the Z-neighbor relation and β²≠1; handle p-divisible discriminants via a minimal positive discriminant and a p-primitive neighbor argument.
Represent the scalar difference F−X₂F in weight (p+1,p+1) by hF−hQ₂F+Q₂(hF), then use the scalar theta injectivity at k=p+1. Do not claim that X₂F is modular of weight (2,2).

Conclude F=X₂F; UX₂=0 and the retained scalar kernel relations, together with (αβ)²≠1, force F=0. Neighbor cycles and Lemma 8.24 supply checks on the coefficient recurrence, not a substitute for all-index contraction.
acceptance: The theta weight is exactly p+1 in the scalar step; an arbitrary large Hasse shift is not interchangeable with it.
The scalar p-primitive/minimal-discriminant recurrence remains an explicit verification obligation.

sources.locator: Theorem 8.22 and §§8.7–8.9, pp.873–877, with the cuspidal restriction and scalar correction
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 8.22 (p.873) states that such constrained q-expansions vanish under the root conditions. Its proof uses binary quadratic forms and neighbour sets (§8.7, Lemmas 8.20–8.21, pp.872–873), the scalar case in §8.8 (p.874, via Θ and Theorem 8.10) and the vector case in §8.9 (Lemma 8.24 and Proposition 8.25, pp.875–877, via θ₁ and Theorem 8.11).

nodes.title: The two Hasse-projection injections
nodes.statement: For cuspidal weight (j,2), j=2 or 4≤j<p−1, residual roots satisfying NR0 and the chosen non-Eisenstein eigensystem, the maps from the selected source to the regular β-part given by e′β∘Aˢ are injective, and likewise with α and β exchanged. This holds at the stated finite coefficient quotients after lifting the residual injectivity through the torsion filtration. It is conditional on the corrected Fourier contraction and scalar kernel obligations recorded in NR4.
proofSteps: Reduce a nonzero kernel modulo ϖ to the constrained systems of NR4/kernel-equations.
Apply cuspidal kernel vanishing in the two distinct weight regimes.
Lift injectivity using successive ϖ-torsion layers and repeat after exchanging the roots.
Use these actual composite injections, rather than bare Hasse multiplication, to obtain the selected image-algebra quotient maps.
acceptance: Both root-labelled injections are required by the unramified-plane argument; a single ordinary line is insufficient.

sources.locator: Theorem 8.13, pp.864–865; reduction pp.867–873; proof completed pp.874–877
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 8.13 (pp.864–865) states that e_β∘A^s and e_α∘A^s are injective from the (α,β)-part in weight (j,2) to the β- and α-parts in a high regular weight. The reduction to q-expansions occupies pp.867–873 and the proof ends in §§8.8–8.9 (pp.874–877).

nodes.title: The unramified ordinary two-plane
nodes.statement: Over each selected finite Hecke quotient in weight (a,2), the regular α- and β-ordinary constructions yield two unramified rank-one local subrepresentations whose reductions are the two specified independent residual lines. They span a rank-two direct summand, invariant and unramified at p, and the symplectic pairing vanishes on it. Thus the two lines yield the precise ordinary local condition in CG20 Definition 4.6(6), not just two unrelated subquotients.
proofSteps: Use the two selected quotient maps to identify the global Galois representation uniquely, then regard both local lines inside this same representation.
Residual independence and Nakayama imply that their sum is a direct summand; verify compatibility with coefficient quotient transitions.
Use the fixed symplectic multiplier and the residual tame-character separation ensured by p−1>a to prove isotropy.
Identify the quotient characters by the pairing and preserve the source ordinary ordering.
acceptance: Two unramified characters appearing only as semisimplified constituents do not suffice; actual stable submodules and their independence are required.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.17 and proof, pp.845–846
sources.match: In the proof of CG20 Theorem 6.17 (pp.845–846), the two surjections from the α- and β-ordinary high-weight Hecke algebras show that r_m|G_p has two distinct rank-one unramified submodules lifting λ(α) and λ(β), and Nakayama's lemma gives the unramified rank-two submodule required by Definition 4.6(6).

nodes.title: Minimal Galois deformation over the singular Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: For a CG lifting datum and every labelled Q, construct a continuous rσ,m:GQ→GSp₄(Tσ(Q)αβ_m), σ=(a,2), lifting r̄, matching the good-prime spin polynomials and satisfying the fixed-multiplier minimal deformation condition outside Q. This includes the split unramified two-plane at p, weakly minimal inertia away p, unramifiedness at q, and inverse scalar inertia on the two isotropic Q-planes. Consequently the universal minimal-outside-Q ring RQ maps to this Hecke image. The theorem depends on the corrected doubling argument.
proofSteps: Construct representations over the selected O/ϖᵐ image quotients by the two regular comparisons and absolute-irreducible reconstruction.
Normalize the full multiplier with the compatible finite-character square root, which uses p odd.
Check the p-condition via the actual two-plane theorem; check each away-p condition via the regular local representation and the finite scalar twist.
Use uniqueness and compatible quotient actions to take the inverse limit, then invoke the supplied universal property of RQ.
acceptance: Do not identify a torsion-ring representation merely from a characteristic-zero product embedding.
The ring map is not yet an isomorphism.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.17, pp.845–846; Definition 4.6, pp.815–816
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 6.17 (pp.845–846) constructs, under Assumption 6.16 and the root condition, r_Q with values in GSp₄(T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_m) that is a minimal deformation of r̄ outside Q in the sense of Definition 4.6 (pp.815–816), using Theorem 8.13, Theorem 6.13 and a square-root twist of the multiplier (p odd).

nodes.title: Klingen block projector and trace
nodes.statement: For the labelled roots of NR0/tw-refinement, let Rx=(xUx,2−α′xγ′x)(xUx,2−β′xδ′x)(xUx,2−γ′xδ′x), and let prx be the compatible factorial-power projector of Rx onto its unit factors. Put prQ=∏x∈Qprx and define the level-raising map prQ∘i from hyperspecial to Klingen level. Let m be the maximal ideal generated by m∅, xUx,2−α′xβ′x, Ux,1−α′x−β′x and ⟨u⟩−1 for u∈ΔQ; without the diamond generators the quotient is only a finite k[ΔQ]-algebra. Use Rx consistently; an undefined R′x is not a separate operator.
proofSteps: Evaluate each polynomial factor on the possible Klingen Satake blocks using the supplied local calculation.
Use the root and product separations to distinguish the desired unit block; apply the upstream factorial-power construction.
Prove compatibility with pullback and trace and multiplicativity across different x.
acceptance: The ideal m is the labelled block lying over the given residual system, not an arbitrary maximal ideal of the enlarged Hecke algebra.
The diamond operators act trivially on H⁰(X₀(Q),·) and unipotently on the p-power covers, so adding ⟨u⟩−1 changes none of the localizations used later.

sources.match: CG20 Theorem 7.2 (p.847) defines, for x∈Q, R_x=(xU_{x,2}−α′γ′)(xU_{x,2}−β′δ′)(xU_{x,2}−γ′δ′), the idempotent pr_x (printed with an undefined R′_x, CG20 extraction E73), pr_Q=∏pr_x and the ideal m generated by m∅, xU_{x,2}−α′β′ and U_{x,1}−α′−β′. Its maximality needs ⟨u⟩−1 in the ideal (design E26).

nodes.title: High-weight Klingen level comparison
nodes.statement: For sufficiently regular shifted weight and the labelled non-Eisenstein block, prQ∘i is an isomorphism on cuspidal H⁰ at the base and Klingen levels. Its inverse is v_Q⁻¹∘tr, where v_Q=tr∘prQ∘i is a p-adic limit of spherical Hecke operators at the primes of Q and is congruent to 1 modulo m∅ under the Taylor–Wiles labelling; d_Q⁻¹tr, with d_Q=[K:K₀(Q)] the degree of X₀(Q)→X, is not an inverse. At each x the characteristic-zero no-newforms calculation is the Genestier–Tilouine Klingen result used by CG20; its integral extension uses torsion-freeness and cohomology/base-change in the vanishing range.
proofSteps: Request the exact local Klingen invariant-vector and eigenvalue computation, not a general Satake theorem alone.
Apply regular-weight cohomological vanishing and identify the integral lattice in the characteristic-zero decomposition.

Show that v_Q=tr∘prQ∘i lies in the completed spherical Hecke algebra at Q, compute it modulo m∅ from the regular residual Satake parameters (each prime contributes d_x·(1/4)≡1, using x≡1 mod p), and deduce that v_Q⁻¹∘tr is an O-integral inverse commuting with h.
acceptance: A characteristic-zero isomorphism alone does not give the integral comparison.
In the GL₂ analogue (q+1)⁻¹tr(prα f)=(qα−β)f/((q+1)(α−β)), which is not f; the degree-normalized trace is not the inverse.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.3 and proof, pp.847–848, invoking Genestier–Tilouine Proposition 11.1.2; inverse corrected as in design E25
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 7.3 (pp.847–848) proves, when the relevant higher cohomology vanishes, that pr_Q∘i is an isomorphism on cuspidal H⁰ with E/O coefficients, following Genestier–Tilouine Proposition 11.1.2. Its claim that d_Q⁻¹tr is the inverse is false and is replaced here by (tr∘pr_Q∘i)⁻¹∘tr (design E25).

nodes.title: Descent through the nonordinary strata
nodes.statement: For the same levels and block, the comparison holds on H⁰ over k in all required weights, on the relevant nonordinary divisor sections, and on H¹ over k, with the inverse v_Q⁻¹∘tr of NR6/high-comparison. Use the h multiplication sequences and a secondary Hasse invariant on the nonordinary locus. Multiplication by h is injective on H⁰ because each connected component of the smooth special fibre is integral and h is nonzero on it; multiplication by the secondary invariant is injective because the nonordinary locus is a Cartier divisor in a smooth threefold, without embedded components, and the invariant is nonzero on each irreducible component. Smoothness alone does not imply irreducibility. The H¹ comparison is proved by reverse induction from the high-weight vanishing range.
proofSteps: Use a cartesian Hasse multiplication square and injectivity of q-expansions to descend the H⁰ comparison.
Apply the secondary Hasse multiplier on the nonordinary divisor; verify its nonzerodivisor property component by component.

Write the two long exact sequences at consecutive Hasse-shifted weights. With H⁰ and divisor H⁰ comparisons established and high-weight H¹=0, descend the H¹ comparison through the exact sequence; do not assert it directly from H⁰.
acceptance: Keep the geometric secondary-Hasse input explicit until its supplier is defined.
The reverse induction must name the starting vanishing weight and every group used by the five-lemma argument.

sources.locator: Lemmas 7.4–7.6 and proofs, pp.848–850
sources.match: CG20 Lemmas 7.4–7.6 (pp.848–850) descend the comparison to H⁰ over k in low weight using powers of the Hasse invariant, to the non-ordinary loci using the secondary Hasse invariant h̃ of Boxer and Koskivirta–Goldring, and to H¹ over k by reverse induction on the exact sequences of h-multiplication.

nodes.title: Finite-level Taylor–Wiles comparison
nodes.statement: For every m≥1, prQ∘i gives the labelled-block isomorphism on H⁰(X,ω(μ)(−D)O/ϖᵐ) and H⁰(X₀(Q),ω(μ)(−D)O/ϖᵐ), with inverse v_Q⁻¹∘tr (not d_Q⁻¹tr). Passing to the direct limit yields the E/O comparison of CG20 Theorem 7.2. BCGP21 Proposition 7.9.8 supplies a separate ordinary-module coinvariant comparison under its own setup; its proof uses derived cohomological comparisons. Neither that proposition nor this degree-zero theorem is exported here as an unrestricted all-degree isomorphism.
proofSteps: For m=1 use the established H⁰ comparison and the H¹ comparison over k.
For m>1 use the exact coefficient sequence 0→k→O/ϖᵐ→O/ϖᵐ⁻¹→0 and the two long exact cohomology sequences, with the H¹ control needed to compare the connecting maps.
Check compatibility with the transition maps, then pass to E/O and dualize only after recording the direction of the maps.
acceptance: The degree-one input cannot be omitted from the induction.
Do not label this result an all-degree isomorphism.

sources.match: CG20 Theorem 7.2 (p.847) states that pr_Q∘i is an isomorphism from H⁰(X,ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})_{m∅} to H⁰(X₀(Q),ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})_m, and its proof (pp.850–851) inducts over O/ϖ^n with Lemmas 7.4 and 7.6 and the five lemma. Appendix A.3.2, Lemma A.6 (pp.887–888) treats Taylor–Wiles vanishing through BCGP21 Proposition 7.9.8 (p.222), whose setting is Hypothesis 7.8.1 (p.211).

Appendix A.3.2, Lemma A.6 (pp.887–888) treats Taylor–Wiles vanishing through BCGP21 Proposition 7.9.8 (p.222), whose setting is Hypothesis 7.8.1 (p.211).

nodes.title: The dual coherent Taylor–Wiles module
nodes.statement: For L=ω(1,3−a) and a quotient Δ of ΔQ, define the coherent homology module MΔ=H₀(XΔ(Q),L)m as the O-dual of H⁰(XΔ(Q),ω(a,2)(−D)E/O)m via the supplied integral Serre duality convention. The bundle identity is ω³⊗L∨(−D)=ω(a,2)(−D). Put S=O[Δ]. Keep this full module distinct from its eαβ-summand. In the source range use p>a−2, with the stronger p−1>a imposed in the final theorem.
proofSteps: Import coherent homology, completed duals and integral Serre duality from the proposed integral coherent supplier.
Calculate the two weights using the actual duality formula, including the cusp boundary.
Transport the Hecke/diamond action with its contragredient convention and preserve the αβ labels.
acceptance: No theorem about balance of MΔ is silently inherited by an idempotent summand.

sources.match: CG20 §7.2 (p.851) defines H_i(X_Δ(Q),L) as the Pontryagin dual of H^i(X_Δ(Q),(ω³⊗L∨(−∞))_{K/O}) and takes L=ω(1,3−a), so that ω³⊗L∨(−∞)≅ω(a,2)(−∞), using p>a−2. Theorem 7.11 (p.853) identifies H₀(X_Δ(Q),L)_m with the dual of the cuspidal H⁰ and studies it as an O[Δ]-module.

nodes.title: H² vanishing and torsion-free coherent homology
nodes.statement: Assume H²(X₀(Q),ω(a,2)(−D)k)m∅=0. Then H₁(X₀(Q),L)m is O-torsion-free by the supplied duality and coefficient sequence. For the balance calculation this vanishing is needed at X₀(Q), not at every intermediate XΔ(Q). For the final minimal theorem retain its stated uniform H² hypothesis for i=0,1 and all required Taylor–Wiles Q. The a≥4 vanishing theorem is imported with its full good-prime and weight hypotheses; in weight (2,2) this remains an assumption.
proofSteps: The coefficient sequence and H² vanishing imply divisibility of H¹ of the E/O-valued dualizing cusp bundle.
Duality turns divisibility into absence of ϖ-torsion in H₁.
Use the supplier vanishing theorem for a≥4 in its actual range. Do not infer full H² vanishing from an interior-cohomology expectation.
acceptance: The uniform condition used in NR8 and the narrower condition used in the balance proof are separately recorded.

sources.locator: Assumption 7.7, Remark 7.8 and Lemma 7.9, pp.851–852; Theorem 5.1, pp.822–823; Theorem 9.1(6), p.878
sources.match: CG20 Assumption 7.7 (p.851) assumes H²(X_Δ(Q),ω(a,2)(−∞)_k)_m=0, Remark 7.8 notes that it holds for p≥a≥4 by Theorem 5.1 (pp.822–823), and Lemma 7.9 (pp.851–852) deduces that H₁(X_Δ(Q),L)_m is p-torsion free. Theorem 9.1 hypothesis (6) (p.878) is the uniform version.

nodes.title: Defect reduction and whole-module balance
nodes.statement: For S=O[Δ] and MΔ as in NR7, assume the H² vanishing at X₀(Q), the supplied Hochschild–Serre identification (MΔ)Δ≅H₀(X₀(Q),L)m and the surjection H₁(X₀(Q),L)m→Tor₁^S(MΔ,O). Let r=rankO H₀(X₀(Q),L)m. The defect dS(MΔ)=dimk(MΔ/mS MΔ)−dimk Tor₁^S(MΔ,k) is nonnegative if dimE H₁(X₀(Q),L)m,E≤r. The localized boundary/Arthur theorem supplies equality of the characteristic-zero dimensions. Hence the full MΔ is balanced, with all classification assumptions retained.
proofSteps: Use the supplied homological Hochschild–Serre low-degree exact sequence with its actual direction; bound the O-rank of the Tor term by the torsion-free H₁ rank.
Reduce the S-module defect to the displayed characteristic-zero inequality using the precise Tor coefficient sequence from R03.5.

Import localized subcanonical/canonical agreement, exclusion of Arthur types (b)–(f), the general-type limit-of-discrete-series contribution and dim H¹=dim H⁰ from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. These moved targets are not replanned here.
acceptance: Show the exact rank/defect calculation; a qualitative appeal to Hochschild–Serre is insufficient.
This conclusion concerns the full module only.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.11 and proof, pp.853–855; Lemma 7.10, pp.852–853, imported under the ownership amendment
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 7.11 (pp.853–855) proves that M=H₀(X_Δ(Q),L)_m is balanced over S=O[Δ] in the sense of Definitions 3.1–3.2 (p.811). The dual Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence gives M_Δ≅H₀(X₀(Q),L)_m and a surjection onto Tor₁^S(M,O), Lemma 7.9 gives torsion-freeness, and Lemma 7.10 (pp.852–853) with Arthur's classification reduces the inequality to dim H¹≤dim H⁰ in characteristic zero.

nodes.title: Balance of the selected Hecke summand
nodes.statement: Under the final lifting hypotheses prove dS(eαβMΔ)≥0. Required additional input: an integral eαβ action on the coherent complex or on H₀ and H₁, commuting with diamonds, duality and the Hochschild–Serre comparison, together with the characteristic-zero rank inequality on this very summand. Whole-module balance alone is insufficient. This is the unresolved selected-summand proof obligation in the final patching argument; the endpoint is conditional on it.
proofSteps: Construct the geometric normalized p-actions integrally in the needed degrees and compare their idempotents through duality and the cover spectral sequence.
Apply the rank/defect calculation to the selected exact sequence, not to the full sequence followed by an unsupported inference.
Either prove the selected characteristic-zero H¹/H⁰ inequality, or give an independent direct proof of selected-module balance.
Until these steps are supplied, retain the conditional balance hypothesis in every theorem using this patching module.
acceptance: An abstract finite O[Δ]-module may have nonnegative total defect while a direct summand has negative defect.
The generic idempotent-splitting theorem does not itself construct a geometric p-action in degree one.

sources.locator: Theorem 9.1 proof, step (c), p.880; Theorem 7.11, pp.853–855
sources.match: In step (c) of the proof of CG20 Theorem 9.1 (p.880), H_N is the (α,β)-part of the dual cuspidal H⁰, but its balance is cited from Theorem 7.11 (pp.853–855), which concerns the whole localized module; Lemma 8.8 (p.860) constructs the operators at p in degree zero only (design E5; CG20 extraction E131).

nodes.title: The nonregular balanced patching datum
nodes.statement: For qTW=dimk of the dual Selmer group, choose labelled QN of cardinality qTW with x≡1 mod pᴺ and a quotient ΔN≅(Z/pᴺ)^qTW. Let HN be the dual selected cuspidal module at the corresponding ΔN-cover; H is its base-level counterpart. The supplied presentation gives R∞=O[[x₁,…,x_(qTW−1)]]→RQN→Rmin, with qTW≥1 justified by the fixed-multiplier Selmer dimension formula. Equip HN with the compatible S_N=O[ΔN] and R∞ actions. Their augmentations identify (HN)ΔN≅H. The modules are finite balanced by NR7/selected-balance, conditional on its explicit proof obligation.
proofSteps: Take the exact CG fixed-multiplier Taylor–Wiles rings and presentation from the global supplier; do not substitute a GLn polarized problem with different real-place dimensions.
For each QN use the nonregular Galois representation and the selected dual module to construct compatible actions.
After the fixed-multiplier twist, inertia is diag(χ,χ,χ⁻¹,χ⁻¹) and χ⁻²=⟨u⟩. This proves the diamond action factors through the deformation-ring action.
Identify the augmentation kernel using universal inertia matrix entries; scalar identities in the Hecke image alone do not prove the universal-ring assertion.
Use the degree-zero level comparison for the coinvariants and the selected balance theorem for the defect condition.
acceptance: Verify the exact diamond-inertia exponent and that augmentation recovers Rmin.
The finite modules may have torsion; no unproved global torsion-free Hecke-ring claim is used.

nodes.title: Conditional minimal R = T and freeness
nodes.statement: For a CG lifting datum, the uniform hypothesis H²(Xi(Q),ω(a,2)(−D)k)m∅=0 for i=0,1 and all required labelled Q, the classification input and the corrected doubling and selected-balance proof obligations, the classifying map Rmin→Tσ(∅)αβ_m is an isomorphism. The O-dual of H⁰(X,ω(a,2)(−D)E/O)αβ_m is a finite free module over this Hecke algebra. Its rank is positive because Katz modularity supplies a nonzero residual selected section. All conditional inputs are part of the theorem contract.
proofSteps: Apply the imported balanced-module patching theorem with the verified ring-action, augmentation and defect data.
Obtain freeness over Rmin; use the nonzero residual module to rule out rank zero.
The Hecke image acts faithfully by definition; a positive free Rmin-module has faithful Rmin-action, so the surjective classifying map has zero kernel and Rmin=T.
acceptance: Keep the two unresolved proof obligations and classification hypotheses in the endpoint; do not mark weight (2,2) unconditional.

nodes.title: The a≥4 minimal theorem
nodes.statement: For 4≤a<p−1 in the same fixed-multiplier residual setting, the supplied coherent vanishing theorem discharges the uniform H² hypothesis. With the corrected doubling, selected-balance and classification inputs, deduce minimal R=T and dual cuspidal freeness at the §6.3 level, including q. Absolute irreducibility and the global cyclotomic multiplier remain hypotheses. Neatness may be deduced from CG Assumption 4.1(H1) with its explicit scalar witness, rather than added to the introduction theorem without explanation.
proofSteps: Check that the vanishing range covers both levels and every Q used by the patching construction.
Give the neatness witness from the cyclotomic/ad⁰ field condition, or retain Assumption 4.2 if that implication has not been established in the supplier interface.
Identify the actual §6.3 level and cuspidal Hecke image in the introduction notation.
acceptance: No unspecified level N(r̄) replaces the actual q-enlarged minimal level.

nodes.title: Arithmetic examples and excluded conjectures
nodes.statement: Check the level recipe on the source genus-two Jacobian example: Iwahori at 5 and paramodular at 3 and 19. Its proposed nonliftable mod-2 weight-(2,2) class is an illustration of conjectural modularity, not an application of the odd-p minimal theorem. The exceptional S₆≅Sp₄(F₂) identification is imported from finite classical-group theory. For Res_K/Q(E), with K imaginary quadratic and E non-CM, the eventual big-image illustration requires E and its conjugate to be nonisogenous over K̄. Weight-(2,2) interior-H² vanishing and the Hecke-ring torsion-freeness expectation remain unproved and unused.
proofSteps: Separate the arithmetic level calculation from the conjectural existence of a mod-2 modular eigensystem.
Import the finite-group exceptional isomorphism rather than construct it in the lifting roadmap.
Request the Weil-restriction open-image theorem from its proposed owner, with geometric nonisogeny.
Use the two regular root lines and the zero-root factor to explain the scalar-weight tripling phenomenon without asserting classicality of every p-adic lift.
acceptance: A mod-2 illustration cannot be used to test a p≥5 lifting theorem.
Do not introduce a dependency from the classification registry ML.0 back to this endpoint.

sources.match: CG20 Remark 4.12 (pp.819–820) argues that Res_{K/Q}E has big image for E without CM and not isogenous to its conjugate. §5.4 (pp.831–832) discusses mod-2 torsion classes through S₆≅GSp₄(F₂) and a Jacobian of conductor 3·5³·19 needing Iwahori level at 5 and paramodular level at 3 and 19. §1.2 (p.804) states the H² expectation, Remark 6.14 (p.842) the torsion-freeness expectation, and Remark 8.18 (p.871) the tripling of weight-(2,2) eigenforms.

nodes.title: Classical modularity from the minimal theorem
nodes.statement: Let r:GQ→GSp₄(Q̄p) have a stable lattice with a CG residual lifting datum, ordinary crystalline local representation at p with Hodge–Tate multiset [0,0,a−1,a−1], and the corresponding minimal away-p ramification. For 4≤a<p−1 and the corrected theorem inputs, r is the Galois representation of a cuspidal Siegel eigenform of weight (a,2) at the stated minimal level. State the Hodge–Tate convention explicitly: ε has weight −1, so the representation with multiplier ε^(1−a) has weights 0,0,a−1,a−1. The good-prime Euler polynomials agree. Equality of every bad Euler factor requires the separate full local–global compatibility theorem.
proofSteps: Use the classifying O-valued point of Rmin and transport it through R=T.
Pass from its characteristic-zero eigensystem to a cuspidal characteristic-zero section using coherent base change in the proved range; identify the attached representation by good-prime uniqueness.
Use the assumed crystalline condition where Frobenius unit roots and the classical ordinary comparison require it.
State the Euler-factor consequence only at the primes covered by the proved local comparison.
acceptance: Ordinary plus numerical Hodge–Tate weights is not a replacement for the required crystalline hypothesis.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1, p.802; Theorem 9.1, pp.878–880, with the crystalline and level qualifications
sources.match: CG20 Theorem 1.1 (p.802) asserts modularity of an irreducible r with ordinary Hodge–Tate weights [0,0,j−1,j−1], the root condition on the unit roots of D_cris, Sp₄(F_p) in the residual image, unipotent inertia away from p and residual modularity, as a consequence of Theorem 9.1 (pp.878–880). The deduction is not written in the paper (CG20 extraction E3).

nodes.title: Pilloni ordinary admissibility data
nodes.statement: An ordinary admissibility datum in the P12 branch consists of p≥5, N prime to p, K⊃K(N), either K neat or p≥7, and an ordinary cuspidal eigenform f of weight κ₀ with its residual Galois system. Require absolute irreducibility (a strengthening of the source’s irreducibility wording), SYMP (the invariant nondegenerate bilinear similitude form is unique up to scalar and alternating), and the exact P12 §5.7 image conditions. These are ζp∉L₀ for the adjoint fixed field; for every m a four-distinct-root σ∈GQ(ζpᵐ) having eigenvalue 1 on every irreducible adjoint constituent; dim H⁰(GQ,gsp₄)=1 and H⁰(GQ,gsp₄(1))=0. Impose the well-ramified χℓ, ε₂, ε, TR local conditions and their chosen tame levels, and strong ordinarity for the ordered four local characters. Fix the flag orientation explicitly before identifying the automorphic and deformation versions.
proofSteps: Specialize the supplier residual pairing, ordinary flags and local deformation conditions; do not identify these image conditions with CG20 H1–H3.
At χℓ primes use two isotropic inertia-character planes, χℓ nontrivial and ℓ−1 prime to p, with strict Klingen level; ε₂ uses Klingen and ε uses Iwahori; TR requires irreducible inertia and p∤ℓ⁴−1.

The automorphic definition excludes λ̄r/λ̄r′ equal to 1 or ε̄ for r>r′; the deformation paragraph prints the reverse index direction. Record and resolve that orientation discrepancy in the supplier comparison rather than treating the two predicates as identical.
acceptance: This branch has no dyadic case and does not use the CG weight-(a,2) balanced module.
Admissibility includes the actual automorphic seed, not only an abstract residual representation.

Definitions 5.1–5.3 (pp.19–20) define the types χ_ℓ, ε₂, ε, TR, well-ramified representations and the FOR condition, printed with r<r′. §5.7 (pp.23–24) states (H1)–(H3), and §7.1 (pp.35–36) defines admissible triples (f,K,p) with p≥5 and K neat or p≥7.

nodes.title: Variable-weight ordinary R = T
nodes.statement: For a P12 admissibility datum with the flag-orientation comparison established, let R̃ be the supplied universal variable-weight ordinary minimal deformation ring and T̃ the localized ordinary cuspidal Hida Hecke image over its two-weight Iwasawa algebra Λ. The natural map R̃→T̃ is an isomorphism; T̃ is finite flat over Λ and the dual ordinary module M̃ is finite free over T̃. For every integral weight κ lifting the residual weight, T̃⊗Λ,κO→Tκ is an isomorphism. These are p-adic ordinary family conclusions, not a claim of classicality in every specialization.
proofSteps: Use the supplied horizontal Hida control theorem to build fixed-weight finite free O[ΔQ] modules and identify their augmentation with the base module.
Verify the equality of diamond and universal-inertia actions, then apply the defect-zero Taylor–Wiles criterion supplied by the commutative-algebra roadmap.
At each integral κ obtain fixed-weight Rκ=Tκ and freeness.
Use finiteness, constant rank and density of integral weights over Λ to prove the family isomorphism, flatness and module freeness, without using the singular coherent balance theorem.
acceptance: The source orientation discrepancy is a named hypothesis until the local comparison is verified.

sources.locator: Theorems 7.1–7.2 and §7.3, pp.36–37 (author pagination)
sources.match: P12 Theorem 7.1 (p.36) states that R̃→T̃ is an isomorphism, that T̃ is flat over Λ and M̃ free over T̃, and that T̃⊗_{Λ,κ}O≅T_κ. §7.2 (pp.36–37, Theorem 7.2) proves the fixed-weight R=T by Taylor–Wiles systems and Fujiwara's criterion, and §7.3 (p.37) passes to the family.

nodes.title: Modularity as an ordinary p-adic form
nodes.statement: Let ρ:GQ→GSp₄(O) have the same residual representation as the P12 seed, inertia isomorphic to the seed at every v∤p, and an ordinary local filtration of weight iκ′=(0,2−k₂′,1−k₁′,3−k₁′−k₂′), for integral κ′=(k₁′,k₂′). Under NR9/ordinary-family-rt, ρ is attached to a cuspidal ordinary p-adic eigenform f′ of weight κ′ and level K. Overconvergence, when supplied by ordinary analytic continuation, is recorded separately from classicality.
proofSteps: The local and residual conditions define an O-valued point of R̃ over κ′.
Transport the point through R̃=T̃ and use Hida control to obtain the p-adic cuspidal eigenform.
Identify the full Galois representation by absolute irreducibility and the good-prime polynomial identities.
Use an actual analytic-continuation theorem if overconvergence is claimed.
acceptance: For κ′=(2,2), the conclusion remains p-adic; the 2025 classicality branch needs additional geometric and multiplicity inputs.

P20's introduction (pp.5–6) recalls this result.

nodes.title: Parallel-weight parabolic ordinary lifting
nodes.statement: For a parallel-weight P12 seed and the corresponding GL₂-parabolic ordinary space, let Λ′ be its one-weight Iwasawa algebra and R̃′ the universal well-ramified ordinary deformation ring with its unique ordered flag satisfying λA,0|Ip=1 and λA,2/λA,1=ε. Then R̃′≅T̃′ is finite flat over Λ′ and M̃′ is finite free. A lift with seed inertia and parallel weight (0,2−k′,1−k′,3−2k′) is attached to a GL₂-parabolic ordinary cuspidal p-adic form of weight (k′,k′). Here GL₂ denotes the parabolic in the genus-two construction, not a change to a rank-two Galois representation.
proofSteps: Use the supplied parabolic horizontal-control theorem instead of the Borel Hida theorem.
Impose the two explicit inertia-character relations in the same universal ordinary deformation framework.
Repeat the fixed-weight and weight-density steps over Λ′, preserving the rank-four symplectic representation and the chosen tame level.
acceptance: Do not transfer a regular-weight classicality assertion to the parallel singular specialization.

sources.locator: §7.4 and Theorem 7.3, pp.37–38 (author pagination)
sources.match: P12 §7.4 and Theorem 7.3 (pp.37–38) treat parallel weight through the GL₂-parabolic ordinary family over Λ′, with λ_{A,0}|I_p=1 and λ_{A,2}λ_{A,1}⁻¹=χ_p, giving R̃′≅T̃′ finite flat and M̃′ free, and p-adic modularity for lifts of parallel weight (0,2−k′,1−k′,3−2k′).

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero weight-two patching data
nodes.statement: A BCGP characteristic-zero datum consists of p≥2 and ρ:GQ→GSp₄(O), unramified outside finitely many primes, with multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, ordinary semistable of weight two and p-distinguished at p, with a chosen p-stabilization (αp,βp). Require ρ(GQ(ζp∞)) integrally enormous in Definition 7.1.1, meaning absolute irreducibility on E⁴ and, for every simple E[H]-submodule W⊂E⊗ad⁰ with H=ρ(GQ(ζp∞)), existence of h∈H whose reduction has four distinct roots and whose action on W has eigenvalue 1. For p=2 require ρ̄(GQ(i))=ρ̄(GQ); for odd p require a regular-semisimple element in ρ̄(GQ) outside Sp₄(Fp). Choose the neat prime r>5 with ρ itself unramified at r, residual regular-semisimple Frobenius, r≢1 mod p if p is odd and r≢1 mod 4 if p=2. Order its symplectic Frobenius roots as αr,1,αr,2,rαr,2⁻¹,rαr,1⁻¹.
proofSteps: Specialize the global and local deformation objects with the exact weight-two ordinary semistable condition and chosen unramified plane.
Use the integral enormous-image condition of this source, which is not ACC+ enormous image; the latter has different mod-p adjoint cohomology conditions and cannot be substituted at p=2.
Choose the neat r under the appropriate odd/dyadic congruence and verify unramifiedness of ρ, not merely of ρ̄.
acceptance: The definition is independent of CG20’s small-weight and odd-p conditions.

sources.locator: Definitions 7.1.1–7.1.2 and Hypothesis 7.1.3, pp.152–154; Definition 7.4.1, p.167
sources.match: BCGP25 Definition 7.1.1 (p.153) defines integrally enormous subgroups and Lemma 7.1.2 gives the Sp₄ and SL₂×SL₂ examples. Hypothesis 7.1.3 (p.153) lists the running assumptions: multiplier ε⁻¹, residual absolute irreducibility, integral enormity over F⁺(ζ_{p∞}), purity, ordinary semistable weight-two p-distinguished local representations with a chosen p-stabilization, ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_{F⁺}) if p=2, and a regular semisimple element outside Sp₄(F_p) if p>2. Definition 7.4.1 (p.167) defines neat primes r>5 at which ρ is unramified; its congruence is misprinted at p=2 (design E16).

nodes.title: Four localized higher-Hida multiplicity modules
nodes.statement: Let S={r}∪Ram(ρ) and retain its p-part, and choose tame compacts Kℓ (hyperspecial outside S, Iw₁(r) at r). At QN use Iwahori and pro-p-Iwahori levels, with ΔQN=∏ℓ∈QN((Fℓ×)(p))² modulo the fixed center convention. For each of the four genus-two Weyl chambers w separately, construct the higher-Hida dual module M_w and auxiliary M_N,w over ΛGSp₄,Q using (7.4.6), the partial central condition before the full character |·|², and localization at the common anemic ideal, the r-refinement and the p-ideal (Up,0−1,Up,1−αp,Up,2−αpβp). The two torus characters of the ordinary deformation define its Λ action.
proofSteps: Use the supplied four higher-Hida complexes and duality; impose exactly the stated central and smooth torus conditions.
Localize successively at the good polynomial and central system, at the r-refinement, and at the normalized p-eigenvalues.
At each QN identify the rank-two diamond torus per prime; do not reuse the rank-one Klingen diamonds of CG20.
Keep all four w modules individually named through base change and patching.
acceptance: The fixed-center partial character condition is part of the construction; taking full central eigenspaces too early can destroy the projectivity argument.

It holds for p=2 as well as odd p; no averaging by the genus-two Weyl-group order 8 is used.

Carry out the Λ[ΔQN] specialization through the supplied projectivity-compatible maps.

nodes.title: Symplectic coefficient descent in every residue characteristic
nodes.statement: Let S⊂R be complete local noetherian rings with m_R∩S=m_S and the same residue field k, of any characteristic, including 2. Let Γ be profinite and ρ:Γ→GSp₄(R) continuous, with ρ mod m_R absolutely irreducible, tr ρ(Γ)⊂S and multiplier ν∘ρ(Γ)⊂S^×. Then ρ is conjugate, by an element of GSp₄(R) congruent to 1 modulo m_R, to a representation with values in GSp₄(S) and the same multiplier.
hypotheses: S⊂R complete local noetherian, m_R∩S=m_S, common residue field k of arbitrary characteristic
ρ continuous, residually absolutely irreducible, with traces in S and multiplier in S^×
proofSteps: Conjugate ρ by some B≡1 mod m_R into GL₄(S) by the GL coefficient descent of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants Layer 1.5 ([CHT08] Lemma 2.1.10), which has no restriction on p; call the result ρ′.

ρ′ and ν·(ρ′)^{−t} are S-valued, residually absolutely irreducible and have equal traces, so Carayol's lemma (same layer) gives A∈GL₄(S) intertwining them. Over R, Schur's lemma makes A an R^×-multiple of the transported form BJBᵗ, which is alternating; since S⊂R, A is alternating over S (zero diagonal, Aᵗ=−A). No division by 2 occurs.
Choose a symplectic basis of the nondegenerate alternating S-form A (possible over any local ring) to conjugate ρ′ into GSp₄(S) with multiplier ν∘ρ.
By Schur's lemma ([CHT08] Lemma 2.1.8) the composite conjugating element lies in GSp₄(R) and is congruent to 1 modulo m_R.
acceptance: At p=2 this replaces the odd-p symplectic descent of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants Layer 1.5, whose cited argument splits invariant forms into symmetric and alternating parts.
The hypothesis that the multiplier is S-valued is used; for Hecke-valued representations it holds because the central Hecke operators lie in the Hecke image.

sources.locator: Lemma 7.4.8 and proof, p.170 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: BCGP25 Lemma 7.4.8 (p.170) states that a continuous ρ:Γ→GSp₄(R), residually absolutely irreducible, with traces in S and multiplier in S^×, is conjugate into GSp₄(S); the proof descends in GL₄ by [CHT08, Lemma 2.1.10], transports the alternating form and chooses a symplectic basis, and the text describes it as Gee–Geraghty Lemma 7.1.1 adapted to allow p=2. The step that produces the alternating form over S is implicit and is supplied here by Carayol's lemma.

nodes.title: Deformation action on the higher-Hida modules
nodes.statement: For every N,w construct the Λ[ΔQN]-algebra map RSQN→TSQN classifying the interpolated symplectic Galois representation with the full multiplier ε⁻¹ and the source’s local ordinary and tame conditions. The maps commute with augmentation to RS→TS and with the actions on M_N,w and M_w. At p=2 the descent step uses NR10/dyadic-descent (BCGP25 Lemma 7.4.8) in place of the upstream odd-p symplectic descent.
proofSteps: If the localized module is zero, use the unique algebra map to its zero image. Otherwise argue as in BCGP21 Theorem 7.9.4: the Hecke image embeds in a product of fields given by dense regular classical points, the product of their GSp₄-valued representations has traces and multiplier in the Hecke image (the central operators lie there), and NR10/dyadic-descent descends it to the Hecke image for every p.
Verify ordinary local characters and every tame local deformation condition, then apply the universal property.
Check the two diamond actions agree and pass to the full-center specialization.
At p=2 no further supplier is needed for the descent: NR10/dyadic-descent holds in residue characteristic 2.
acceptance: Dense field-valued points do not automatically provide an integral GSp₄-valued representation over a nonreduced ring.
