nodes.title: Projective Satake comparison and diamond coinvariants
nodes.statement: On the regular residual Satake block, use the projective finite-group module comparison of Lemmas 7.4.11–7.4.12 to identify spherical and selected Iwahori invariants without dividing by 8. After partial-central specialization and then the full central character, (M_N,w)ΔQN≅M_w equivariantly for RSQN→RS. This is the exact augmentation comparison required in Hypothesis 7.2.1(4).
proofSteps: Apply the norm/invariants/coinvariants comparison only to the supplied projective finite-group module.
Calculate the regular Satake block at each auxiliary prime and verify that the selected character factor is the spherical one.
Impose the central conditions in the order used by the projectivity theorem, then identify the augmented Hecke and Galois actions.
acceptance: A blanket assertion that invariants commute with quotient or base change is not valid here.

sources.match: BCGP25 Lemmas 7.4.11–7.4.12 (pp.171–172) compare spherical and Iwahori invariants through projective modules over the finite group algebra, and Lemma 7.4.15 (p.173) identifies the Δ_{Q_N}-coinvariants of M_N with M compatibly with R_S^{Q_N}→R_S.

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero local freeness
nodes.statement: Let q⊂RS be the characteristic-zero prime defined by ρ. For each w, (M_w)q is a finite free (RS)q-module, with rank possibly zero. Apply the abstract characteristic-zero patching theorem to the finite Λ[ΔN]-free modules with compatible augmentation. Its proof must use a cofinal system of open ideals suitable for both the weight variables and diamond variables, a constructed compatible action of the patched deformation ring, the cotangent bound, and a justified lift through the completed regular local ring. These extra proof obligations are recorded explicitly; the printed assertion that powers of the augmentation ideal alone form the needed cofinal system is insufficient.
proofSteps: Request the corrected abstract patching construction from the commutative-algebra owner, with open ideals containing weight/maximal-ideal powers and large enough diamond kernels.
Construct the ring action before using the patched module; compare the quotient topology with the module topology.
At q invert p, use the bounded relative cotangent module to get the completed-ring surjection. Justify the S∞-algebra lift and the dimension/depth calculation with the same coefficient ring.
Apply Auslander–Buchsbaum and specialize the augmentation to obtain finite local freeness.
Do not infer automorphy, positive support, global freeness or rank one at this stage.
acceptance: The proof obligations on the patched ring action and lift remain open supplier contracts; this target is conditional on them.

nodes.title: R-regular classical weights
nodes.statement: For an integer parameter R≥1 and ordered integral Hodge–Tate weights h₁,h₂ of the two ordinary torus characters, RRegularWeight(R,h₁,h₂) means h₂−h₁≥R and 1−2h₂≥R. For a weight-space point also require that the two inertia characters are algebraic with these weights. The light numerical predicate is separate from the existence of those algebraic characters.
proofSteps: Use a positive natural bound R and the existing integer carrier for the two inequalities; transport the resulting condition to the supplied weight-space characters.
Derive monotonicity in R and preserve the order of the two characters.
acceptance: Do not replace the second inequality by a difference of the weights, or apply the predicate to arbitrary smooth characters.

nodes.title: The dyadic and odd-prime automorphic seeds
nodes.statement: For NR10 data require one of two seed alternatives. A: p=2, a solvable CM extension F/Q and ordinary RACSDC π on GL₄/F with r̄π,2≅ρ̄|GF, nearly adequate residual image over F, a residual regular-semisimple element there, a strongly residually odd polarized pair (ρ̄|GF,1) at an infinite place of F⁺, and ρ̄(GQ(i))=ρ̄(GQ). B: p>2, an ordinary cuspidal GSp₄/Q seed π with central |·|² and ρ̄π,p≅ρ̄, GSp₄-reasonable and tidy residual representation, a regular-semisimple element outside Sp₄(Fp), and compatible p-stabilizations such that the seed local representation lies on a unique ordinary component and ρ lies on that same component. The initial matching is residual, not equality of the target p-adic representation with an automorphic one.
proofSteps: Use the residual image and polarized-oddness notions from their supplier APIs with their actual coefficient fields.
Record all five conditions in each alternative and the exact residual restriction field.
In alternative B include the unique-component property for the seed local representation in addition to shared component membership.
acceptance: Do not strengthen residual matching to p-adic matching in a way that would assume the conclusion.
Nearly adequate, reasonable and tidy are separate imported predicates with definition-level supplier requests.

nodes.title: Multiplicity one at a nonzero regular point
nodes.statement: Choose Kℓ=Par(ℓ^a(ρ|GQℓ)) at ℓ∉{p,r}. Let q′ be a characteristic-zero point on a common irreducible component of RS[1/p] with q. For sufficiently large R, if q′ has R-regular classical weight and (M_w)q′≠0, then dimE(M_w/q′M_w)[1/p]=1 for each w. The nonzero hypothesis is essential; this theorem does not construct a classical point in the support.
proofSteps: Use regular arithmetic control to identify the fiber with the sum of cuspidal automorphic representations having the same Galois point and the specified refinements.
Use localized boundary/interior comparison and global multiplicity one for general-type packets; these are supplier inputs, not new classification theorems here.
At ℓ≠p,r use the unique generic paramodular newvector at the conductor and constancy of the relevant pure local conductor on the component.
At p use the one-dimensional simultaneous ordinary refinement eigenspace of the regular principal series; at r use the one-dimensional selected Iwahori block and residual regular semisimplicity.
acceptance: A point on another local deformation component is not covered by the conductor/refinement argument.

sources.locator: Proposition 7.5.1 and Lemma 7.5.2, pp.174–175; equation (7.5.5) and Lemma 7.5.8, pp.176–177

nodes.title: Support through the singular point
nodes.statement: With NR10 data and one seed alternative, prove (M_w)q≠0 for all four w by exhibiting a deformation component through q contained in Hecke support. The dyadic route uses ordinary unitary deformation finiteness and regular automorphy lifting after solvable CM base change, followed by solvable descent. The odd-prime route uses the component selected by B5 and regular GSp₄ ordinary automorphy lifting. Only the component through q is required; no global identification of all reduced deformation components with the Hecke algebra is asserted.
proofSteps: Request the precise regular ordinary automorphy-lifting/finiteness theorems from the proposed ordinary modularity-lifting Part II owner, including the dyadic near-adequacy and local component hypotheses.
Use finiteness and the dimension lower bound to make a component through q dominate the relevant weight component, then prove density of regular arithmetic points there.
Apply the appropriate regular automorphy theorem at those points and the source’s solvable descent Proposition 7.5.3 to put them in Hecke support.
Pass from dense supported points to support of the selected component; since M_w is finite and locally free at q, infer its positive local rank.
acceptance: This is the nonvanishing proof; local freeness alone gives no support.

The regular lifting theorems are an explicit missing interface (regular ordinary support gate) and the solvable descent is requested from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7; neither is hidden in the word seed.

nodes.title: Rank one at the weight-two point
nodes.statement: Under the running NR10 data, the complete seed alternative and the corrected patching/supplier proof obligations, (M_w)q is finite free of rank one over (RS)q for every one of the four w. The deduction combines local freeness, positive support through q and a sufficiently regular nonzero classical point on a relevant component; it does not equate total rank across the four chambers with one.
proofSteps: Use finite local freeness at q to obtain a neighborhood on which each module has constant rank.
Choose a dense R-regular arithmetic point on the supported component in that neighborhood.
Apply regular multiplicity one at this nonzero point and identify the free-module fiber dimension with the constant rank.
Repeat for each w, retaining all four one-dimensional fibers.
acceptance: The argument needs the regular point in the free neighborhood and in support, not merely somewhere on the deformation space.

sources.locator: Proposition 7.5.10 conclusion and final proof paragraph, pp.177–179

nodes.title: Ordinary weight-two modularity lifting
nodes.statement: Assume NR10 data, the full dyadic or odd seed alternative, the explicit corrected patching and interpolation proof obligations, and either Zariski image containing Sp₄ or image containing SL₂×SL₂ with ρ irreducible and becoming reducible over an index-two subgroup. Then ρ is the representation of a classical cuspidal Siegel modular form of weight (2,2). Use the local semistable weight-two hypothesis to supply de Rhamness and the four rank-one multiplicities to verify the higher-Coleman classicality criterion. The theorem is not obtained by removing the H² hypothesis from CG20’s integral R=T theorem.
proofSteps: At q use the arithmetic specialization/control theorem to obtain the ordinary overconvergent eigensystem with the same full good-prime data.
Use isotypy to identify its completed eigenspace with ρ⊗W, not just an unspecified four-dimensional representation.
The four rank-one graded pieces give equal multiplicities n=1 and total dimension 4. Semistability gives de Rhamness and semisimplicity of the required Sen operator.
Apply the imported classicality theorem; retain the classification/packet input used to pass from higher-degree classicality to the degree-zero cusp form.
Compare the geometric and dual-spin conventions before concluding that the form realizes the original ρ.
acceptance: Classicality requires both de Rhamness and the four matching multiplicities.
All unresolved source and supplier gates of NR10–NR11 propagate to this endpoint.
